title: The Names of the Divine and the Garments
description: T52 names three registers at which the Lord goes forth: gods (called from the Lord's inmost), rich-men (called by the gods, the first living word), and angels (called by the rich, the embassy sent to all who stand in stillness). One Lord recognized at three depths, each summoned out of the one above. T53 describes how the Divine Human goes forth clothed: love alone is enough to quench the proprium's foolishness, but four further accommodations attend it as helpers — thought, truth-in-natural-degree, wisdom in receivable form, and the medium of perception. In doing this work love takes a wound; the Lord's principles dwell together with one another in concord, while the proprium is one of a single self-loving practice. Souls follow the Lord upward by agreement of practice, scattering darkness; what does not agree must perish.
